Browsing anonymously requires no personal data. If you create an account, Clerk provides the sign-in interface and manages your credentials, authentication sessions, and session tokens. Awesome Video does not receive or use your password for sign-in. Clerk sends us the identity details needed to connect your account, including your account identifier and, when available, your email address, name, and profile image. We store a local account record with those details, your role, and your activity on the site: bookmarks, favorites, learning-journey progress, preferences, and resource submissions. A nullable password field retained from the site's pre-Clerk authentication system may remain on legacy account records, but it is not used for authentication.

name.value: We use Google Analytics 4, Mixpanel, PostHog, and Amplitude to understand how the site is used, including page visits, popular resources, interactions, performance, and errors. PostHog and Amplitude may also provide session-replay features; PostHog masks page text and all form inputs in those recordings. These services only load after you accept analytics in the consent banner, and you can decline without losing site functionality.

name.value: Our hosting platform, Replit, also provides Replit Analytics, which counts page visits without cookies or cross-site identifiers. Unless you decline analytics in the consent banner, the site also sends Replit Analytics anonymous interaction and performance events — for example, which resource or related link was opened, page-load timings, whether a submission, sign-up or sign-in completed, the address of a page that was not found, and the kind of error the site hit. These events never include your name, email address, account identifier, or the text you type. Page-visit counts are recorded by the platform whether or not you decline.

name.value: Infrastructure cookie set by our hosting edge (Google App Engine), not by this application. It supports request routing between the edge and our servers — we do not use it to track you, it carries no analytics, and we never read it. Because it comes from the hosting platform, it appears on your first visit regardless of your analytics consent choice. It applies site-wide (path "/"). You can block or delete it in your browser settings at any time — the site keeps working; the edge may simply set a fresh one on a later visit.
